notes: Baseline contamination: without_skill runs read in-repo rule files (ai-skill-inbox/README.md, check-plugin.sh, common-skill-guide/SKILL.md) from the working directory, so the baseline is 'no skill but with org docs'. The skill's effect is under-measured.

Eval 1: without_skill scored higher (93% vs 73%). with_skill runs stop at the folder-path question per SKILL.md §1 and never show push/PR commands (A5 failed 3/3); with_skill run-2 did not say the reviewer must be an individual (A4). Baseline runs warned explicitly that naming the lead-<team> team is ignored.
Eval 2: with_skill 100% vs without_skill 89%. Caveat: with_skill run-1 and run-2 grep results surfaced the skill's own eval criteria (contamination).

Eval 3: both 50% on every run. A1 ('answer immediately with SUM') is unpassable because executors were told to ask and stop when input is missing; A2 is non-discriminating. Neither assertion measures whether the skill was wrongly triggered.
Time/tokens: with_skill was faster (45s vs 83s) and used fewer tokens, mainly because the baseline searched the disk and read rule docs.

Safety: real tool-call logs of all 21 executor transcripts (incl. 3 failed attempts) contain zero executed git/gh commands. 3 runs were re-run after API safeguard errors; failed outputs kept in the session scratchpad.
